critical_failures.symptom: The python script to generate speech training inputs and compile lexicon dictionaries is unpublished. Users cannot run the alignment pipeline on custom or new audio recordings.
critical_failures.remedy: None from public resources. Re-implementing the script would require reproducing CMU Sphinx training setup and classical Arabic G2P rules from scratch.

critical_failures.symptom: The tool cannot align a continuous surah audio file. It fails if the input file contains silent pauses between verses because it expects pre-cut EveryAyah-formatted clips as its absolute inputs.
critical_failures.remedy: An external VAD or acoustic segmentation layer must pre-process and chop the continuous audio into verse clips before passing them to quran-align.

critical_failures.symptom: If any word in the reference text is missing from the precompiled phonetic dictionary, PocketSphinx fails to construct the decoding graph and crashes.
critical_failures.remedy: Ensure absolute coverage in the .dict file for all text variations, or implement a rule-based grapheme-to-phoneme backup generator.

critical_failures.symptom: The acoustic model relies on per-reciter speaker adaptation (SphinxTrain). Running it on an unseen or untrained reciter results in extremely poor alignment bounds and high state deletion rates.
critical_failures.remedy: Train a universal classical Arabic deep neural network acoustic model (e.g., using Kaldi or Wav2Vec2) rather than using GMM speaker-adaptation templates.
